# From commit to merge

After a Cursor plugin install, the short command loop is [plugins/crav1/README.md](../plugins/crav1/README.md).

## First prompt

```text
/crav1-finalize-commit
```

It drafts first, then offers commit, copy, change, or stop (1.83.0: there is no opening question).

```text
/crav1-finalize-commit message-only
```

`message-only` drafts and shows the Summary and Description, then stops, the same as picking copy.

```text
/crav1-finalize-commit commit-now crav1
```

`commit-now`, or just `commit`, drafts, shows the Summary and Description, then commits without the choice question. `/crav1-finalize-commit commit-now` may still ask one question: which work item to mention, when `work-item.md` has several Feature lines and none clearly matches the slice. It is one card, at most 4 options plus a typed Other, and the mention is never copied from `git log` or the previous commit. It never pushes. When `agent-tools/` or build output is in the file set, it warns and offers the normal choices instead. `crav1` (CRAV1 style) or `git-log` (match the repo's log) answers the style question for this commit; a saved style rule still works as before.

```text
/crav1-finalize-commit pull
```

## Steps

| Step | You | Agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Commit style (first time) | Pick CRAV1 style or the style of this repo's git log, once or onward | Asked in the same question as the commit choice, with the message drafted in the recommended style; never before the draft (1.89.0). Asked at most once per run (1.90.5). Onward writes a commit-style rule so you are not asked again. Delete the rule to choose again |
| Draft | — | Reads the diff, recent `git log`, the commit-style rule, and `docs/specs/<slug>/work-item.md` when it exists. Drafts a Summary and Description. A work item id becomes the last description line: `#<id>` on Azure Repos, `AB#<id>` on GitHub |
| Commit | Pick commit, copy, change, or stop | `/crav1-finalize-commit` offers commit first. After the commit, it checks the message, and when a host or tool added any trailer or line to that unpushed commit (Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Aider, Codex and other listed tools), strips those known tool trailers once, keeps `Signed-off-by` and a real person's `Co-authored-by` (1.94.0) and keeps the work item line. `/crav1-finalize-commit` commits only when you also asked for that in the same turn |
| Pull request | `/crav1-open-pr`, then pick push and open, open only, or stop | Shows the title and the body (since 1.176.0 a short fixed shape: a 2–3 sentence summary, one line per task with its full name and what it does, 1–2 lines on how it was verified, and the work-item mention; no links at all) before asking. Pushes only after an explicit yes. Opens one pull request against the default branch. Does not merge |
| Review (optional, later turn) | `/crav1-review-pr <pull request>` | Reads the diff against the spec, plan, and `verify.md`, and says whether it can ship. Writes nothing. See [From a pull request review](from-review-pr.md) |
| Merge (later turn) | `/crav1-merge-pr <pull request>` and say merge | Merges only when that turn asks. Always a merge commit: no squash, no rebase, no policy bypass. Stops when a required host check is red. Confirms two parents, then fast-forwards the local default branch when the tree is clean. Does not run the review |

## What gets written

- The commit-style rule, when you pick onward.
- `.githooks/commit-msg` and the trailer-hook answer, when you pick strip trailers.
- The git commit, when you pick commit.
- A push of the change branch and one pull request, after a yes.
- A merge commit on the host, when you ask to merge.

## On a base branch (1.99.0)

When you are on `main`, `develop`, the `Merges into` branch or a `release/*` branch and anything staged is code (outside `docs/` and the root Markdown files), `/crav1-finalize-commit` never commits there, even with `commit-now`. Its one prompt becomes `Commit on a work branch?`: **Create feat/<slug> from <into> and commit (Recommended)**, **Use an existing branch**, or **stop**. A typed branch name is that card's free-text answer, hint `Type a branch name`. `new-branch` answers it in one line.

## Trailer hook (1.90.0)

The first time `/crav1-finalize-commit` runs in a repo without the hook, its one prompt also asks: Strip tool trailers on every commit for this repo? `strip-trailers` adds `.githooks/commit-msg`, runs `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, and saves the answer, so it never asks again. The hook removes only the known tool trailers (Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Aider, OpenAI Codex, Gemini, Jules, Devin, Windsurf, Amazon Q, Cline, Amp and JetBrains AI; 1.94.0), even from tools that ignore their own attribution setting. A co-author line for a real person, such as `Co-authored-by: Ada Example <ada@example.com>`, and any `Signed-off-by` line stay. `keep-trailers` saves no and adds nothing.

Where `/crav1-finalize-commit` has no questions tool, it asks in plain text: numbered lists, one per question, ending with `Reply with choice words in one line, e.g. commit once strip trailers.`.

## Behind, conflicts, or a rejected push (1.66.0)

The kit's advice is always to merge the base branch into your branch, never to rebase it:

- `/crav1-merge-pr` stops when the branch is behind the base or has conflicts, and says: `Merge develop into feat/orders-retry (resolve any conflicts there), push, then ask to merge again.` A `walk-progress.md` conflict that is only version lines is settled by the same stamp rule as `/crav1-finalize-commit`. On GitHub, **Update branch** with **Update with merge commit** does the same for a branch that is only behind.
- When a pull request is already open for the branch (since 1.114.0), `/crav1-open-pr` pushes after your yes, then shows the commits added since the description was written and asks: **update description**, **add as comment**, **push only** or **stop**. On someone else's pull request, **add as comment** comes first. Either text is shown in full before anything is posted. The card is `yes (Recommended)` to post it as shown, or typed changes on that card's free-text answer, for example `drop the second bullet`. Nothing is posted until you say yes. The comment reads as a normal reviewer comment: what was pushed and why.
- `/crav1-open-pr` shows the error when a push is rejected because the remote branch moved, and says to pull with `git pull --no-rebase`, resolve any conflicts, and push again. A `walk-progress.md` conflict that is only version lines uses the same stamp rule. It never force-pushes.

```text
git switch develop
git pull --ff-only
git switch feat/orders-retry
git merge develop
git push
```

## Shared pull-request steps (1.158.0)

`/crav1-open-pr`, `/crav1-merge-pr`, `/crav1-pr-status` and `/crav1-review-pr` share one page for the steps they have in common: which pull request a number or URL names, the host order (GitHub, then Azure DevOps, then printed steps), Windows quoting, the open state, claims, catching up by merging the base in (never a rebase), signing in (since 1.177.0 the CLI advice names only the host the pull request is on), and the run ending. One read-only script, `scripts/pr_common.py`, does the lookups: `parse` (which host and number), `resolve` (since 1.177.0, a bare number is looked up in the kit's records first: build-progress, the merge list, PR notes and `repos.md`, before this checkout's remote; several candidates means it asks), `find` (the open pull requests for one branch, never picking the newest), `checks` (passing, failing and pending), `claim` (the `In progress:` lines for a branch) and `behind` (how far behind the base, with the merge-in advice). It never pushes, posts, merges or writes `claims.md`. Nothing changes in what you see: `/crav1-merge-pr` still merges only on your explicit ask, always with a merge commit, and `/crav1-build-walk` still clears its own claim after the merge.

## Someone else pushed first (1.81.0)

After the commit, `/crav1-finalize-commit` fetches. It never pushes.

- **Behind:** it runs `git pull --no-rebase --no-commit`, never a rebase and never an automatic merge commit. Conflicts in specs, system files and notes are resolved by the kit's rules: both sides' new lines are kept (yours first), each repo and branch keeps its newest `Synced at` line, an `Approved:` line under `## Approval needed` is never dropped, and the note indexes are rebuilt rather than merged. The rebuild is part of the merge commit, noted in that commit's message. It runs the nothing-lost check and says nothing was lost only when that check passes. If a line is missing, it does not commit. Then one merge commit. No third commit for the index.
- **Walk progress:** a conflict in `walk-progress.md` that is only version lines (`Tasks version` and the other hashes) is settled in that same merge. The script takes the upstream text and writes the merged file's hash when the recorded hash matched that side and the only difference is progress (a checkbox, a `(PR n)`, a line ending). A real sentence change keeps the upstream hash, so the walk reopens the steps that change affects. `Done` and `Result` stay. If a conflict also touches `Done` or `Result`, it stops and names the stamp-only hunks. Say `settle stamps` to resolve those lines and leave the rest. It does not push.
- **Build progress:** a `build-progress` file is settled the same way when the conflict is only hash lines. A `(live yes: …)` note counts as progress. `/crav1-finalize-commit` runs that settle and does not push.
- **Unfinished walk:** the next line is `/crav1-tighten-and-plan-ready-to-build`, because the walk paused. An unfinished build walk comes next. that is a Run next entry with the command that resumes it, such as `/crav1-build-walk orders-api feat/orders-cicd` for a whole-branch run, or `/crav1-build-walk orders-api T3` for one task, not a `Next:` line. That comes before `/crav1-open-pr`.
- **Base branch:** it says to push `main` or `master`, because a pull request cannot open from that branch into itself. On a feature branch the next line names `/crav1-open-pr`.
- **A real disagreement:** when both sides changed the same line in different ways, you get one question: keep both (theirs becomes a `**Conflict:**` line under yours), mine, theirs, or stop.
- **Code files:** conflicts there stay with you, as before.
- **Not behind:** it checks any merge you have not pushed yet, including one you resolved by hand. A merge that kept your `**New:** Retries stop after 3 attempts` line but silently dropped the other side's `**New:** Retries back off for 30 seconds` line is listed, with restore / show me / stop. After `restore` the restored lines go into this run's commit, with the one confirm at the end.

`/crav1-finalize-commit pull` does the same without committing first. With uncommitted changes it stops and names `commit` instead.

## PR note (1.65.0)

`/crav1-open-pr` does not save the body it drafts: that is its own summary. When an infra, pipeline or PROD change states no rollback, the chat says `No rollback stated` (the body does not). `/crav1-pr-status` takes the merge order from the ready check and `build-progress/`, and the questions from the spec's open questions, not from the body. After a confirmed merge, `/crav1-merge-pr` writes or updates the pull request's PR note in the specs repo (`docs/notes/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD-pr-<repo>-<n>.md`, its title and description, `kind: pull request`), with any edits made to the description since, and sets its PR record's `State` and `Ready` lines to merged. Before merging it reads the `Ready` line and stops on `no` unless you say `anyway`. A review with `/crav1-review-pr` writes the same note. From the specs repo, a pull request in another repo is reviewed with `/crav1-review-pr <repo> <n>`.

`/crav1-finalize-commit` shows the draft and the choices from the skill file. The commit steps are read only after `commit` or `commit-now`.

## After

After an outside pull request merges, `/crav1-review-pr` names `/crav1-refresh-system-notes` to catch the picture up: [Keep the picture current](from-refresh-system-notes.md).

Reference pages: [finalize-commit](reference/skills/crav1-finalize-commit.md) · [finalize-commit](reference/skills/crav1-finalize-commit.md) · [open-pr](reference/skills/crav1-open-pr.md) · [merge-pr](reference/skills/crav1-merge-pr.md)

The run ends as [How a run ends](reference/run-ending.md) says: Run next, never a `Next:` line. After the commit it is `Push the specs repo:` with `git push`, `Push and open the pull request:` with `/crav1-open-pr`, or `Push to PR <n> and comment:` with `/crav1-open-pr pr<n>`; `/crav1-open-pr` ends with `Review PR <n>:` and `/crav1-review-pr <repo> <n>`, after a `git push` catch-up when the specs repo is ahead; `/crav1-fix-build-gaps` ends with commit and push catch-ups before verify. `Waiting:` only when a step is blocked, and `Uncommitted:` when files changed and are not committed.

every finalize-commit ending is Run next or nothing: `commit`, `copy`, `stop`, and a failed commit never print a `Next:` line. A suggestion to throw an edit away is a plain sentence, for example: To throw the edit away, run `git checkout -- docs/specs/orders-api/build-map.md`. A typed `commit` still asks, with `stop` recommended, when the only changed files are kit-rewritten files (`build-map.md`, `walk-progress.md`, `build-progress/*`) whose values disagree with `verify.md`, such as a done commit on the build map.

a pull request description from `/crav1-open-pr`, on GitHub and on Azure DevOps, is a short fixed shape: a 2–3 sentence summary of what the branch delivers, one line per task with its full name and what it does, one or two lines on how it was verified, and the work-item mention. On Azure DevOps `pr_common.py fit --body <file> --text` is only a guard for the 4,000-character limit: when a body is still too long it shortens the task lines and adds the plain line `Task lines were shortened to fit.`

a teammate whose repo already has `.githooks/commit-msg` but whose git config does not point at it is asked in the same choices prompt, `turn-on-hook` or `skip-hook`, before `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` runs. The config is never changed silently.

every Run next example starts with its reason line, for example `The commit is only local.` above `Push the specs repo:` and `git push`.

## 1.199.0 changes

`/crav1-finalize-commit commit-push` commits and then pushes once the fetch check says nothing was lost: one yes for both, never a force push. An `Uncommitted:` line names the command in a code span.

## 1.200.0 changes

`scripts/ending.py --vendor copilot` prints the ending from the shared helper, Run next first. When a `design/<topic>` branch is checked out or owns the change, the helper shows a stay card and never offers the default branch.
